notes: Correct, and it adds static folding of string concatenation, but it keeps the checked AST and walks it on every round trip in the hot path instead of precomputing at provision. The tests are strong, including an end-to-end retry using a direct ph() call.

The detection is correct and resolves concatenated string literals at compile time, but it keeps the checked AST and re-walks it on every proxied response in the hot path instead of precomputing at provision; its tests are good, including a direct ph() retry test.

Behaves correctly and is precomputed at provision, but it hardcodes reverse_proxy placeholder names into the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher as an exported, proxy-specific method, which is a layering smell. The doc edit also drops the mention of {rp.is_transport_error}.

The fix is correct: the AST is walked at provision time, names are matched exactly, the header prefix is handled, and dynamic names are treated as conservative; however, reverse_proxy-specific placeholder names are hardcoded in the generic caddyhttp matcher, a redundant value-type switch case is added, and the doc no longer mentions is_transport_error.

Correct and well tested, using provision-time placeholder extraction with a dynamic flag, deduplication and an exact-name check. The extra value-type MatchExpression case is unnecessary, and the API doc comment was edited, though relevantly.

It exposes a clean, generic Placeholders()/dynamic API that is computed once at provision time, and the response-name logic correctly stays in reverseproxy; minor nits are the redundant value-type case and returning the internal slice, offset by thorough tests in both packages.

Matches the reference design: placeholder names are collected from the checked AST at provision time, non-literal names are flagged as dynamic, and reverseproxy holds an exact list of response placeholders plus a header prefix. Tests cover the CEL and reverseproxy layers and a POST integration case; the only nit is that the internal slice is returned without cloning.

A clean provision-time extraction via MatchDescendants/FunctionMatcher yields a generic Placeholders() API with conservative dynamic handling, closely mirroring the reference, with focused tests in both caddyhttp and reverseproxy.

Clean and close to the reference: literal names and a dynamic flag are recorded at provision behind a small predicate-based API, and reverseproxy owns the response-placeholder list. It has a thorough detection table (comprehension, transport_error, prefix lookalikes, escaped and plain literals) plus an integration test, but no CEL-level unit test.

Placeholder names and the dynamic flag are precomputed at provision, a small generic predicate API is exposed, and response-specific knowledge stays in reverseproxy; the detection test is broad (comprehensions, prefix look-alikes, escaped literals, non-expression sets) and there is an end-to-end regression test.

A clean, focused fix that mirrors the reference's call sites, including stash show, plus mnemonicPrefix=false; it adds rename/copy-to fallback and single-component stripping with /dev/null and no-prefix handling, and updates the existing command tests.

Sound and well documented. It adds a helper applied to every diff lazygit reads, including stash and the worktree diff, and generalizes prefix stripping, including rejecting a leading '/'. Like most candidates it forces mnemonicPrefix off, unlike the reference. Visible test changes are mostly updated arg expectations.

Moving the prefix configs into AddCommonDiffArgs is a tidy way to cover every rendered diff, stash show included, and the parser changes closely track the reference; this restructures more than needed, and only command-arg test updates are visible.

Fixes the bug by moving a forced a/ b/ prefix config into AddCommonDiffArgs (which also covers stash and the worktree diff) and by making the parser strip any single-component prefix. It also handles rename/copy-to lines. Downsides: it forces diff.mnemonicPrefix=false, overriding a preference the reference deliberately keeps. Hiding config side effects inside AddCommonDiffArgs is somewhat implicit.

Fixes the bug: it forces a/ b/ prefixes (also turning off mnemonicPrefix) at every call site including stash show, and generalizes prefix stripping and rename/copy handling, but it adds an unneeded `Configs` builder helper and rescans the header in a second loop for rename/copy lines.

Correctly forces standard prefixes across all diff commands and generalizes the parser. It adds an unnecessary new Configs builder API, and rename/copy lookup is done in a second loop over the header. It also overrides the user's mnemonicPrefix.

The parser is solid and the tests are strong (header-field, diff --git and header cases plus an integration test), and using --src-prefix/--dst-prefix is valid, but stash show is never given a forced prefix, so the noprefix/custom-prefix requirement is unmet there.

The parser fix is clean and passes --src-prefix/--dst-prefix on the command line, which in effect also overrides mnemonic prefixes. It leaves `stash show` without enforced prefixes, so a stash diff under diff.noprefix can still resolve wrong paths. Tests are thorough: parser unit tests for header fields, diff --git splitting and rename/copy, plus an integration test.

Matches the reference's coverage and also protects the `stash show -p | git apply -R` pipeline in SaveStagedChanges, a genuine same-class bug; the parser changes are clean and the existing command tests are updated.

Same overall approach as the reference, applied broadly. It also hardens the `stash show -p | git apply -R` pipeline in SaveStagedChanges, which fits the maintainer's intent. It overrides mnemonicPrefix rather than leaving it alone. Visible tests are mostly arg-expectation updates.

Fixes the issue by hand-setting callers to cancelling when descendants are unfinished, but also changes UpdateRunJob globally to always refresh the run after every cascade (extra hot-path work, beyond what the fix needs); tests are very thorough, including force and legacy-stuck scenarios.

Writes the caller as cancelling when it has unfinished descendants, but it also makes the hot-path UpdateRunJob always refresh the run, which goes beyond the needed fix and reloads all attempt jobs for each caller; the tests are very thorough, including the force and legacy-stuck cases.

Small, targeted change in cancelOneJob that re-aggregates expanded callers instead of cancelling them outright, plus emitting the run after a settle-only cancel; tests cover the nested handshake via UpdateTaskByState and both cancel and force-cancel; minor wart: the caller row is always returned as updated even when unchanged.

Simple, general fix that re-aggregates any caller with children from their status instead of cancelling it outright, matching the reference semantics, and it emits the settled run; the tests cover the nested acknowledgement and both cancel modes, though the caller is returned even when unchanged.

Works by routing all callers through a new cancelCaller that refreshes from children, but it duplicates the direct-cancel logic, drops the task_id guard and the IsDone short-circuit for callers; its service test verifies end-to-end waiter unblocking, while the model test fakes the ack via a raw UpdateRunJob.

Routes callers through a dedicated cancelCaller that aggregates from children; it slightly duplicates the direct-cancel path (dropping the task_id condition) and needlessly restructures the emit call, but its service test verifies end to end that the waiting run actually starts.

Concise fix that refreshes a caller only when a direct child is cancelling (deep nesting works through the upward cascade); the narrower check relies on that cascade, it always returns the reloaded caller as updated, and the tests check both the ack flow and that the waiter is re-emitted.

Keeps a caller cancelling by re-aggregating it when any direct child is still cancelling, which is enough because callers are processed deepest-first, and emits the run when no job was updated; the main flaw is that it returns the reloaded caller even when nothing changed.

Closest to the reference: inside cancelReusableCaller, expanded callers are re-read (and refreshed if not done) instead of being force-written to cancelled, so they follow their cancelling children; the run is emitted when settling finishes it; the nested ack test is realistic, but the service test only checks that the emit mock was called.
Closest to the reference: it reloads each expanded caller, re-aggregates it, and reports it only when its status changed, plus emits the run when it settles; the tests are focused and concise.

Gets reconnect-on-request and close-on-failure right, but resets engine params to configured values via new unexported struct fields rather than forcing fresh discovery; that changes `GosnmpWrapper`'s shape and likely caused the failed hidden test.

Like C2 it restores configured engine params rather than always rediscovering, failing a hidden test; it also leaves the localized keys in place when restoring a configured ID, so keys can mismatch the engine ID; the plugin-side close and its tests are fine.

Restores configured engine params through added struct fields (failing one hidden test), adds an unrelated production `mibDirFS` rewrite of MIB loading, and adds no test that `Gather` closes the connection on error.

On reconnect it restores the configured engine ID/boots/time instead of forcing discovery, which diverges from the spec and fails a hidden test; the new unexported struct fields break positional GosnmpWrapper literals, it adds an unrelated production rewrite of the gosmi MIB loader, and it has no test for close-on-error in the input plugin.

The SNMP fix is correct and has excellent tests, including a mock v3 agent that changes its engine ID, but it rewrites production MIB loading (`appendPath` via `AppendFS`, abs paths, vanished dirs read as empty) to work around a test-environment path issue, which is unrelated scope creep.

The wrapper and plugin fix is essentially the reference, and the mock-agent test proves end-to-end rediscovery; but it bundles an unrelated production change to mib_loader.go (filesystem registration, abs-path conversion, ignoring missing dirs) to work around an environment issue.

Matches the reference closely: `Close` is in the interface, `Get`/`Walk` reconnect first, `Reconnect` clears USM engine state and localized keys, and `Gather` closes the connection on field or table failure; good tests across v1/v2/v3 and a gather test with failing and healthy agents, though it edits the unrelated `TestSnmpInitGosmi` path as an environment workaround.

Closely matches the reference (Get/Walk reconnect, Reconnect clears engine params and keys, plugin closes immediately on field/table failure) with solid wrapper and plugin tests; the only stray edit is a test-only tweak to TestSnmpInitGosmi.

Correct wrapper reset (engine ID, boots, time, keys, context engine ID) plus a deferred single close on any gather failure; strong tests verify a real discovery packet is sent after reconnect, with only a minor unrelated `TestSnmpInitGosmi` tweak.

Reconnect resets USM state, keys and ContextEngineID, and Get and Walk reconnect first, so the core fix is sound; but closing is deferred to the end of the agent goroutine, so later tables in the same gather keep using the stale session, and it also edits the unrelated TestSnmpInitGosmi.

Works for the specified flows, including root-at-symlink, copy and the hostile case, but the squashfs New/NewObject retry logic and the zip Open EOF special-casing are convoluted, and a symlink can be listed with the same name as a regular .rclonelink file.

Close to the reference: zip appends the suffix and reads the member, and squashfs exposes the StatT target, but the NewObject and New remote-matching logic is convoluted, the zip Open past-end special-casing is clunky, and symlink/regular name clashes are not handled.

Thorough and correct, with shared helpers, the local-style needs-suffix error for a root that names a symlink, shadowing protection and bounded target reads; it does add exported API to archiver plus a binary fixture, reads targets eagerly, and the tests swap the global logger.

Thorough, consistent implementation for both backends with shared OpenLinkTarget, regular-file shadowing and root-at-link support mirroring local's needs-suffix error, plus extensive tests and docs; one small inconsistency remains in NewObject for symlinks whose own name ends in .rclonelink.

Clean fix close to the reference: zip reuses the member data as the target with an offset clamp, squashfs List and NewObject agree, a regular .rclonelink member shadows a same-named symlink, docs are added, and tests are good though the squashfs ones need mksquashfs.

Clean, consistent implementation in which regular .rclonelink members shadow same-named symlinks, root-at-link works in both backends and List agrees with NewObject; it adds good zip and archive-level copy/escape tests and docs, though the squashfs tests depend on mksquashfs being installed.

The zip side is fine and close to the reference, but squashfs New double-appends the link suffix to f.file when root names a symlink (so its listing comes back empty), a missing StatT gives an empty target silently, and the tests include duplicated assertions.

The basic listing, lookup and reading work, but a squashfs root pointing at a symlink gets a double .rclonelink suffix in f.file and lists nothing, a missing StatT silently yields an empty target, and the escape test checks the wrong location.

A LinkFilter is well-intentioned hardening, but it silently drops symlinks with nested members and even regular .rclonelink members, case-insensitively; that contradicts the spec and fails a hidden test.

Covers the whole feature and keeps List and NewObject in agreement in squashfs via a shared dirEntries, but its LinkFilter drops clashing symlinks and even some regular .rclonelink members, which contradicts the 'listed under name+suffix' and 'stays a regular file' requirements, adds a lot of extra machinery, and fails a hidden test.

The core translation works in both backends, but the zip side goes further than the spec and drops any symlink that has members under it or clashes with another entry; this deviation fails a hidden test, and every symlink target is read eagerly at listing time.

Squashfs handling is sound, but zip drops any symlink that has members inside it or clashes with another entry, using a hacky addLinks that writes nil dirs and calls CheckParents twice; this diverges from the expected listing semantics and fails a hidden test.

Close to the reference: closes the leaked dup fd, adds a closed CAS returning net.ErrClosed, unlinks the stored address under unixSocketsMu only on the last release, and skips abstract sockets; it keeps the pre-existing closed-newest-first reuse issue, as the reference does, and has solid tests.

Minimal fix that closely matches the reference: closes the leaked dup fd, unlinks the real address under unixSocketsMu when the count reaches zero, adds a CAS-guarded double close returning ErrClosed and skips abstract sockets, with good targeted tests.

Replaces the per-holder map entry with a shared master-fd and refcount struct, which looks behaviorally sound and even fixes the closed-newest-first reuse bug; but the rewrite of internal types breaks the hidden white-box tests (0/7, suite fails), and the '@' check is applied on every OS.

A clean master-fd plus atomic-count redesign that also fixes reuse after the newest holder closes, but it rewrites internal types (breaking all hidden tests), checks '@' without a GOOS guard, and leaks a pool ref on its new error path.

Clean shared-socket struct with good error-path cleanup and a NUL/'@' path helper, but it restructures internals and deleteListener beyond what was needed and is incompatible with the hidden tests (0/7, suite fails).

A well-reasoned shared-socket redesign with error-path cleanup, a careful abstract/NUL path helper and a guarded deleteListener, but the internal refactor goes beyond what was needed and is incompatible with the hidden tests (0/7).

Largest rewrite: new mutex, restructured listenReusable, reuse path now wrapped in deleteListener and counted in listenerPool, plus a listeners.go edit; the reasoning is careful but it goes far beyond the issue, and it fails every hidden test along with the package suite.

The ref-counting logic looks right, but this is the most invasive patch: a second mutex, a restructured listenReusable, changed listenerPool accounting for reused sockets, an edit to listeners.go, and an abstract-socket check with no GOOS guard; it fails every hidden test.

Master-fd refcount design with a reference-compatible isAbstractUnixSocket, but it removes the unixListener mapKey/count fields and adds unrequested deleteListener pointer/closed changes; the hidden suite fails (0/7) and the second Close returns a wrapped OpError rather than net.ErrClosed itself.

A sound redesign: a shared unixSocket keeps a master fd and a ref count, the unlink happens under the lock, abstract sockets are handled and double-close is guarded, but replacing the map type and wrapper structs broke compatibility, so 0/7 hidden tests pass and the package suite fails.
